label: Lasting joy
title: Bhagavad Gita on Happiness: 7 Verses on Lasting Joy
description: Seven verses on happiness that lasts: joy from within (5.24), the pleasure that sours (18.38) and the joy worth working for (18.37). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try.
h1: Bhagavad Gita on happiness: 7 verses on lasting joy
subtitle: For keeping a good mood from slipping, and finding the joy that stays. Read one a day, or all seven now.
intro: The Gita has a clear view of happiness. Some joy starts sweet and turns bitter (18.38). Some starts hard and ends like nectar (18.37). These verses begin with the person who is happy from within (5.24), tell the two kinds of joy apart, show where the lasting kind lives (5.21, 2.65), and end with two practices: choosing the harder joy and keeping a gentle mind (17.16). The last is from the Yoga Vasishtha, a crow who lived through the ages and stayed happy.

image.alt: A woman with eyes closed and a quiet smile in light rain on a rooftop as friends laugh behind her
image.altGlobal: A man with eyes closed and a quiet smile on a park bench in autumn sun as friends laugh behind him

days.heading: Lit from within
days.line: Happy within, at ease within, lit from within: that person finds lasting freedom.
days.forYou: Krishna describes someone whose happiness, pleasure and light are all inside: antaḥ-sukhaḥ, antar-ārāmaḥ, antar-jyotiḥ. Good days still come from outside. This joy doesn't depend on them.
days.today: Sit for a minute with your eyes closed, and notice anything in you that feels good right now.

days.heading: Why some joy sours
days.line: Some pleasure tastes like nectar at first and poison in the end. Know which kind you're choosing.
days.forYou: The extra drink, the late-night scroll, the impulse buy. Krishna calls this rājasa pleasure: nectar at first, poison later. Knowing which kind you're reaching for is half the work.
days.today: Catch one 'nectar first' pleasure today before you reach for it.

days.heading: A joy that doesn't run out
days.line: Unhooked from outside pleasures, you find a joy within that doesn't run out.
days.forYou: Outside pleasures end when the thing ends. Krishna points to a joy inside, akṣayam, one that doesn't run out. It grows the more your happiness rests on yourself.
days.today: Spend fifteen minutes on something that needs nothing bought or scrolled.

days.heading: Clear mind, light heart
days.line: When the mind clears, sorrows start to dissolve, and understanding settles quickly.
days.forYou: Krishna's word is prasāda, clarity or serenity. When the mind clears, sorrow loosens its hold on its own. A lot of lasting joy is a quieter mind.
days.today: Clear one small mess today, a drawer or an inbox, and notice how your mind feels after.

days.heading: Choose the joy that starts hard
days.line: Some joy tastes like poison at first and like nectar in the end. That joy is worth it.
days.forYou: Exercise, practice, an honest conversation, a habit you're building. Krishna calls this sāttvika happiness: bitter at the start, nectar at the end. That joy lasts.
days.today: Do one thing today that's hard at first and good in the end.

days.heading: Practise a gentle mind
days.line: A calm mind, gentleness, quiet, self-restraint and a clean heart: that is discipline of mind.
days.forYou: Krishna calls these the austerity of the mind: serenity, gentleness, silence, self-control, a clean heart. Practised daily, they keep a good mood from slipping away.
days.today: Keep ten minutes of silence today, phone away.

days.heading: The crow who outlived the ages

story.title: Bhushunda
story.body: The sage Vasishtha travelled to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who had watched whole ages of the world come and go and was still happy. Asked his secret, Bhushunda listed his habits. He didn't brood on the past or the future. He didn't fret about what he'd get next. Learning never made him proud. And he was glad when others were glad, and sad when they were sad.
story.lesson: A long, glad life comes from staying present, wanting little and staying kind.

verse.sanskrit: सुखितोऽस्मि सुखापन्ने दुःखितो दुःखिते जने । सर्वस्य प्रियमित्रं च तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verse.line: I'm glad when others are glad and sad when they're sad. Being everyone's friend keeps me well.

days.forYou: Bhushunda's last habit is the easiest to start: share in other people's joy. It doubles yours.
days.today: Celebrate someone else's good news today, out loud.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about happiness?
faq.a: 18.36 to 18.39 describe three kinds. Sāttvika happiness is like poison at first and nectar in the end (18.37). Rājasa happiness is nectar at first and poison in the end (18.38). Tāmasa happiness comes from sleep, laziness and confusion. Krishna also describes joy that comes from within (5.21, 5.24).
In 18.37, the happiness that feels like poison at first and nectar in the end, born from a clear and settled mind. Think of the joy of a practice you've kept up.

faq.q: Which Gita verse is about inner joy?
faq.a: 5.24: one whose happiness is within, whose delight is within and whose light is within reaches freedom.
